Astronome et statisticien belge, il appl: A Belgian astronomer and statistician, he applied the bell curve to human measurements and invented the “average man.” We also owe him the index that would become the BMI.
Généticien britannique, il découvre en 1: A British geneticist, in 1984 he discovered genetic fingerprinting while looking at an X-ray film of DNA. In 1986, the method cleared a suspect and led to the real culprit of a double murder.
Physicien italien, il empile en 1800 des: An Italian physicist, in 1800 he stacked discs of zinc and copper separated by cardboard soaked in brine: the first electric battery. He thus continued his dispute with Galvani, for whom electricity came from frogs.
Naturaliste britannique, il conçoit la s: A British naturalist, he conceived natural selection in 1858, feverish, in the Moluccas, and wrote to Darwin about it. Their two texts were read together at the Linnean Society of London.
Psychiatre suisse, d'abord proche de Fre: A Swiss psychiatrist, first close to Freud, he broke with him in 1913. He proposed the notions of introversion and extraversion, and a collective unconscious peopled with archetypes.
Astronome américain, il pilote la concep: An American astronomer, he led the design of the Voyager probes' Golden Record and presented the Cosmos series in 1980. In 1990, he got Voyager 1 to turn around and photograph the Earth: the “pale blue dot.”
Psychologue et journaliste scientifique: An American psychologist and science journalist, in 1995 he popularized “emotional intelligence,” a notion proposed five years earlier by Peter Salovey and John Mayer.
Psychologue israélo-américain, il étudie: An Israeli-American psychologist, he studied with Amos Tversky the biases of judgment and the way we weigh gains and losses. In 2002 he received the Bank of Sweden prize in economics without ever having taken an economics class.
Physicien italien, prix Nobel en 1938, i: An Italian physicist, Nobel Prize in 1938, he left fascist Italy with his wife, who was Jewish. In Chicago, in 1942, he led the first controlled nuclear chain reaction. He loved estimating anything in his head.
Biologiste allemand, il invente le mot «: A German biologist, he coined the word “ecology” in 1866 and drew plates of marine organisms of great beauty. Some of his embryo drawings, too neatly arranged, earned him accusations of fraud.
Juriste et conseiller d'Henri IV, il not: A lawyer and adviser to Henri IV, he denoted unknowns with letters and invented symbolic algebra. He also broke a Spanish cipher, so well that Philip II accused France of sorcery.
Prêtre et physicien belge, il propose en: A Belgian priest and physicist, in 1927 he proposed that the Universe is expanding, then that it was born from a “primeval atom”: the idea that would become the Big Bang. He refused to mix his faith with his cosmology.
Chimiste américain, il propose en 1916 q: An American chemist, in 1916 he proposed that the chemical bond is a shared pair of electrons, and invented the dot notation that bears his name. Nominated dozens of times for the Nobel, he never received it.
Moine à Brno, il croise pendant huit ans: A monk in Brno, for eight years he crossed thousands of pea plants and drew from them the laws of heredity, published in 1866. They remained ignored until 1900.
Psychologue américain, il décrit en 1974: An American psychologist, in 1974 he described “burnout” among volunteers at a free clinic in New York, and in himself.
Médecin hongrois à Vienne, il impose en: A Hungarian doctor in Vienna, in 1847 he enforced hand washing with chlorine and brought down the death rate of new mothers. His colleagues rejected him; he died in an asylum.
Astronome américain, il montre en 1924 q: An American astronomer, in 1924 he showed that Andromeda is another galaxy, then in 1929 that galaxies move away faster the farther they are. He relied on Henrietta Leavitt's method.
Emmanuel Kant, philosophe de Königsberg,: Immanuel Kant, philosopher of Königsberg, a city he almost never left. In the Critique of Pure Reason, he asks what reason can know. His neighbors, legend has it, set their watches by his walk.
Philosophe et économiste allemand, il éc: A German philosopher and economist, he wrote the Communist Manifesto with Engels in 1848, then Capital, prepared over years in the British Museum reading room.
Philosophe autrichien puis britannique,: An Austrian, later British, philosopher, he argued that a theory is only scientific if some observation could refute it. In his view, astrology and psychoanalysis failed this test.
Philosophe britannique, elle imagine en: A British philosopher, in 1967 she imagined the trolley problem to discuss the doctrine of double effect. The example ended up taking on a life of its own.
Savant anglais, il observe le liège au m: An English scientist, he observed cork under the microscope and named the little chambers he saw “cells.” A rival of Newton, he left no authenticated portrait: this one is imagined.
Philosophe et romancière, elle écrit en: A philosopher and novelist, in 1949 she wrote The Second Sex: “One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.” The Vatican put the book on the Index.
Tenu pour le premier philosophe grec, il: Regarded as the first Greek philosopher, he looked for natural rather than divine causes: according to him, everything comes from water. Herodotus credits him with predicting an eclipse in 585 BC.
Philosophe américain, il demande en 1974: An American philosopher, in 1974 he asked “What is it like to be a bat?”: science can describe sonar, not what the bat feels.
Général athénien exilé, il raconte la gu: An exiled Athenian general, he told the story of the Peloponnesian War by cross-checking witnesses, with no gods or omens to explain it. He also described the plague of Athens, which he caught and survived.
Astronome français, il calcule en 1846 l: A French astronomer, in 1846 he calculated the position of an unknown planet from the irregularities in Uranus's orbit. Johann Galle found it the very evening he received his letter: it was Neptune.
Physicien écossais, il réunit électricit: A Scottish physicist, he united electricity, magnetism and light in a single theory in 1865. In 1861 he also had the first color photograph taken, of a tartan ribbon.
Ouvrière du textile et parachutiste amat: A textile worker and amateur parachutist, in 1963 she became the first woman in space, aboard Vostok 6: 48 orbits in nearly three days. The second would fly nineteen years later.
Ami de Montaigne, il écrit très jeune le: A friend of Montaigne, he wrote the Discourse on Voluntary Servitude when very young: a tyrant has only the power that is given to him. Montaigne would say of their friendship: “Because it was he, because it was I.”
